name: SND@LHC
full_name: Scattering and Neutrino Detector at the LHC
summary: SND@LHC is located off axis in CERN LHC tunnel TI18, approximately 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point. Its multipurpose forward-neutrino program officially includes weakly coupled particles that might constitute dark matter.
detection_principle: Dense tungsten targets and emulsion record interaction vertices, with electronic calorimetry and a muon system measuring final states. Weakly coupled dark-matter scattering may resemble neutral-current events and must be separated from neutrino backgrounds.

results.summary: Collider neutrinos have been measured; this is not a dark-matter discovery.
Upgrade studies assess future light-dark-matter-scattering sensitivity; these are projections.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
